title: SynthGraph
summary: A data lineage system that links synthetic-data generators, datasets, training runs and evaluations into one traceable graph.
highlights: Hashed-key authentication, strict domain boundaries and migration discipline
Python SDK and CLI for zero-friction metadata capture
Lineage graph, generation comparison, reproduction manifests and reports across the generator, dataset, training run and evaluation chain
Designed during Hack-Nation Venture Labs and maintained as an independent open-source initiative

narrative.problem: When a model trained on synthetic data misbehaves, the cause often lies upstream of the dataset, in the generator, its seed and its parameters, a step that run-tracking tools such as Weights & Biases and MLflow have no concept of.
narrative.constraints: It stores only lightweight metadata, caller-supplied checksums and URIs, never dataset bytes, frames or model weights, and it stays engine-agnostic: the SDK is a thin client with free-form JSON parameters.
narrative.decision: Model generation, dataset version, training run and evaluation as one queryable lineage, stored relationally in PostgreSQL behind a NestJS API, with a Python SDK and CLI that capture metadata from any script.
narrative.result: A traceable chain from generator to evaluation, with generation comparison, reproduction manifests and reports. The backend is covered by 230+ automated tests gated by CI/CD.

lines: api → persist generation · dataset · run · evaluation
graph → query lineage across the chain
implementation.summary: A thin Python SDK reports metadata to a NestJS API, and PostgreSQL stores the metadata that the dashboard and reports query.

paragraphs: SynthGraph is a data lineage system for synthetic training data. It connects the generator that produced a dataset, the seed and parameters it ran with, the training run that consumed the dataset and the evaluation that scored the result, so that a model that misbehaves can be traced back through that chain instead of guessed at.
SynthGraph was designed and built during the Hack-Nation Venture Labs incubator program and is now maintained as an independent open-source research and development initiative.

Weights & Biases and MLflow track training runs and metrics well, but neither has a concept of what happened before the dataset: the procedural generator, the domain-randomization bounds and the seed behind the data a model trained on.
For synthetic-data and simulation-to-real pipelines, that upstream step is often exactly where a failure originates.
Builder and core maintainer. Owned the system design end to end: domain modeling, API contracts and engineering guardrails across the backend, the frontend and the Python tooling.

constraints.title: Metadata, not data
paragraphs: SynthGraph never touches dataset bytes, render frames or model weights. It stores lightweight metadata, caller-supplied checksums and URIs, and where those URIs point is entirely up to the researcher.

constraints.title: Engine-agnostic by design
paragraphs: The SDK is a thin client: it does not hook into Blender, MuJoCo, Isaac Sim or any other engine, and generator parameters are a free-form JSON object rather than a fixed schema.

The backend is a modular monolith: one NestJS application with explicit feature modules for projects, experiments, generations, datasets, assets, training runs, evaluation results, comparisons, reproduction, reports, search and documentation.

Requests flow from the SDK over HTTPS and JSON through a controller, an application service and a repository to PostgreSQL via TypeORM. Controllers handle HTTP concerns, application services hold use-case behavior and repositories isolate persistence.

technicalDecisions.title: A modular monolith instead of distributed services

paragraphs: One NestJS application with clear module boundaries serves the whole API.

The current scale and product stage do not justify distributed services, so the design deliberately avoids microservices, event buses, Kubernetes, CQRS and event sourcing until a concrete workload requires them.

alternatives.tradeOff: Distribution adds operational and consistency complexity that the current requirements do not repay.

technicalDecisions.title: Lineage as relational data in PostgreSQL

paragraphs: Lineage is represented with foreign keys and junction tables, and JSONB is used only where provenance is genuinely flexible.
The domain has strong relational lineage, ownership, versioning and integrity requirements. JSONB for generator parameters means a new parameter never needs a migration.

alternatives.tradeOff: Not required while the relationship graph stays manageable with PostgreSQL foreign keys and junction tables.

technicalDecisions.title: Hashed API keys and ownership-chain authorization

paragraphs: SDK requests authenticate with API keys that are stored only as hashes, and authorization follows the ownership chain from user to project to experiment to generation or training run.
An identifier alone never proves authorization: every query verifies that the resource belongs to the authenticated user's chain, and multi-tenant isolation is covered by automated tests.
The API stays unversioned as long as every change is additive: a new field or route is added beside the old one rather than replacing it.

The CLI, SDK and frontend all track the backend directly, so a version prefix buys nothing until a genuinely breaking change exists. If one becomes unavoidable, every route moves under a version prefix in the same change.

The backend is NestJS and TypeScript on PostgreSQL, with TypeORM migrations and schema synchronization disabled. A Python SDK captures provenance from inside a research workflow and a CLI queries, compares and exports it afterwards.

A Next.js dashboard and product site sit on top of the same API, using route-based lazy loading with ECharts and @xyflow/react for charts and graphs. Docker Compose starts PostgreSQL, the backend and the frontend with one command; in production the backend runs on Render with PostgreSQL on Supabase.
The backend is covered by more than 230 automated unit and end-to-end tests, run in GitHub Actions together with linting and builds for the backend and the frontend on every pull request.

learnings.title: Architecture first
paragraphs: Designing the system architecture, domain model and boundaries upfront kept the system coherent as it evolved.

learnings.title: Engineering with agentic AI
paragraphs: Building software effectively with agentic AI while keeping architecture, system design, domain modeling and engineering decisions intentional.

learnings.title: Guardrails matter
paragraphs: Clear API contracts and engineering constraints prevent design drift and enable rapid iteration.

learnings.title: Design compounds
paragraphs: Strong foundations and additive API rules enabled rapid iteration without continuously breaking existing functionality.
